startup.name: stratify
startup.one_liner: AI agents that help you understand your customers' needs
startup.description: An AI user researcher that recruits participants, runs interviews, analyzes responses and returns insights. Customers are product, design and research teams paying subscription fees. Two person team in San Francisco. Forecast as of 2025-04-07, window to 2026-11-17 (about 19 months).

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is in the Spring 2025 batch, so this is shown for completeness. Start from the roughly 1 percent prior for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent range). Adjust up for a clear AI moderated interview wedge and a technical two person team; adjust down because several YC companies, including Outset, Rally and Great Question, already hold this space and no traction is stated.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because AI moderated user research already has YC backed competitors with funding and enterprise logos, such as Outset and Rally, plus Great Question and UserTesting. Without a differentiated recruiting panel or paying customers, the partners would see a thin wrapper over interview scripting and summarization.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B gave seed 47% / 53% / 59% (n=1002, cond 53%); --tag "Conversational AI" gave 74% / 78% / 79% but n=19, anecdote only. Time rule: 2022+ months to seed p50 6, p75 14.2, about 85 percent of ever reachers by 19 months.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Ever anchor 0.53 scaled by 0.88 for the 19 month window gives 0.47, cut to 0.40 because of a crowded category with funded YC rivals and a two person team. Below the anchor, no lift for AI theme. The odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: A small post YC round of about $1M to $3M from angels and a micro fund, the most common outcome when a team has early pilots but no repeatable sales motion. It is the largest band because the 2022 and later seed table (p25 $2.0M, median $3.5M) mixes in YC deal sized checks.
A conventional institutional seed of $3M to $6M led by a seed fund, matching the 2022 and later table median of $3.5M and the p75 of $5.2M for the cohort.

A $6M to $12M seed, which happens when a lead fund prices on market heat. Among confirmed 2026 raises above $1M the median was $6.0M, but press covers large rounds more, so this band is kept at a minority.
An upside seed above $12M, reached only if the company shows unusual early revenue or a top fund competes for it; rare in the YC data and kept small.

ladder.why_it_fails: Window is 19 months (2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17); seed means an outside round above about $1M. The most likely miss is that the product is judged a feature: Outset raised a $3.8M seed and Rally an $8.8M seed in April 2024, so investors will ask why a later two person entrant wins. Versive and Monterey AI, small YC teams in feedback and research, did not show a priced round, and Great Question grew slowly on a $2.5M seed.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B gave series_a cond 26% (n=468). Time rule: 2022+ months to series A p25 19.4, p50 28, so under a third of ever reachers close an A inside 19 months.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Ever conditional of 0.26 scaled by about 0.3 for the 19 month window, because most A rounds arrive near 28 months. More than 2x below the anchor for that reason.

bands.rationale: A thin or bridge style Series A of $6M to $10M, common when growth is real but revenue is still small; below the 2022 and later p25 of $11M, so it stands for the soft band.
The central Series A of $10M to $18M, bracketing the 2022 and later median of $15M and p25 to p75 of $11M to $21M.
A larger A of $18M to $30M that top funds lead when growth looks category defining; current market data shows A deal sizes near $17M to $20M.
An upside A above $30M, seen only for a few AI companies with very fast revenue; rare and kept at a small share.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A in 19 months would need enterprise contracts with repeat usage, but market research budgets move slowly and enterprises trial several AI interview tools. Great Question raised only a $2.5M seed in its first year and grew on a small base before a $13M A, and Rally waited about two years after its batch for its seed. A two person team will likely lack the sales capacity to show that growth in time.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B gave series_b cond 21% (n=123). Long run, not window numbers.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Equal to the B2B anchor; long run chance beyond the window.

bands.rationale: A smaller or flat Series B of $15M to $30M, typical when the A cohort slows; includes down or extension rounds.
The central Series B of $30M to $50M, matching the 2022 and later median of $40M with p25 to p75 of $27M to $55M.
A growth B of $50M to $80M for companies with clear scaled revenue.
An upside B above $80M for category leaders, rare among YC companies.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B requires winning the enterprise research budget against UserTesting, Qualtrics and funded AI rivals, and many research teams build only small, project based budgets. Outset's quick rise after its 2023 seed is an exception; a typical tool in this category stalls after an A because buyers consolidate vendors.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B gave series_c cond 19% (n=26); older eras 36 to 43 percent.

bands.rationale: A modest later round of $30M to $60M, including down rounds and structured deals.
The central round of $60M to $120M, bracketing the 2022 and later series C median of $74M.
A large growth round of $120M to $250M for a clear leader.
A mega round above $250M, which only a handful of YC companies have reached.

ladder.why_it_fails: A growth round past B needs a platform that becomes the system for customer insight, which collides with Qualtrics and UserTesting. Most research software companies end with a sale to a larger insights or feedback platform, as with Monterey AI, rather than a Series C.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The likely failure is commoditization: AI moderated interviews become a feature of UserTesting, Qualtrics or Great Question, and a two person team cannot out sell funded YC rivals. User research tools exit small, as Monterey AI to Reforge or a G2 style acquisition suggests, and a $1B outcome would need a category defining platform.

analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a $2.5M seed in July 2021 and a $13M Series A, a capital efficient but slow path; the closest incumbent among YC peers.
Raised an $8.8M seed in April 2024 about two years after its batch, showing a seed arrives late for this segment.
Raised a $3.8M seed and quickly grew with enterprise names; the strongest direct competitor.
Inactive with no funding found; a user research tool that did not grow.
Three people, still operating, no priced round found; shows the small outcome path.
Small team acquired by Reforge around January 2025 with undisclosed terms; a soft exit.

killers.risk: Funded YC rivals and incumbents own the AI interview niche
killers.evidence: Outset and Rally raised seeds and have enterprise logos, while UserTesting and Great Question already serve research teams.
killers.mitigation: Win a vertical such as consumer apps or fintech and own the participant panel.

killers.risk: Quality of AI moderated interviews stays below human research, limiting trust
killers.evidence: Comparisons describe audio only moderators missing nonverbal cues and analysis overemphasizing outliers, which researchers distrust.
killers.mitigation: Publish validation studies against human moderated research and add human review options.

killers.risk: Participant recruiting depends on third party panels and has thin margins
killers.evidence: Recruiting costs are a large part of study cost and Great Question and UserTesting maintain panels at scale.
killers.mitigation: Integrate customer lists and build a proprietary panel in a niche.

competition_now.name: UserTesting
competition_now.what: Incumbent user research platform with its own participant panel

competition_now.name: Great Question
competition_now.what: User research CRM and interview platform from YC W21
competition_now.traction: Raised a seed and Series A and serves product teams

competition_now.name: Outset
competition_now.what: AI moderated customer interviews for enterprises, from YC S23
competition_now.traction: Raised a seed and grew with enterprise customers by 2024

technical_complexity.rationale: Interview scripting, voice or chat moderation, transcription and synthesis are buildable by two people in three months with current language models. The harder parts are recruiting real participants and trust in analysis, not the core technology, so the technical moat is thin.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbent research platforms and funded rivals can add AI moderated interviews within about six months and already own panels and enterprise distribution. The incentive to defend customers is strong, so the takeover risk is high.

evidence.claim: Companies pay for user research tools, and incumbents such as UserTesting serve large enterprise research budgets; AI interview startups such as Outset raised funding in 2023 and 2024.
Research teams want faster qualitative insight; AI moderated interviews are marketed as faster and cheaper than human led research, though these are vendor claims.

roadmap.goal: Show research teams pay for AI interviews
actions: Run 20 paid studies for product teams
Compare insight quality against human moderated interviews
roadmap.proof: 10 paying teams and a quality benchmark

roadmap.goal: Repeatable subscription revenue with a niche panel
actions: Pick one vertical and own its participants
roadmap.proof: $20K to $40K monthly recurring revenue and 80 percent logo retention

roadmap.goal: Move from project spend to platform budgets
actions: Add continuous research and integrations to product tools
roadmap.proof: $1.5M ARR and 120 percent net revenue retention

pros.point: Clear workflow pain and active buyers
pros.evidence: Product and design teams buy research tools and AI interview startups raised funding in 2023 and 2024.

pros.point: Low build cost for a two person team
pros.evidence: Core stack is available through current language and voice models, so a small team can reach a usable product quickly.

brand.name: stratify
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "stratify" --era 2022+ gave kind suffix_coinage (ends in ify), 8 characters, 3 syllables.
weaknesses: The word is used by other data and analytics products
brand.rationale: A suffix coinage that hints at layers of insight works as a plain business name, but it is not distinctive and shares its stem with other analytics companies, so the effect is neutral and does not move the ladder.

narrative.headline: A reasonable idea in a category that already has funded YC rivals; seed is plausible but below the base rate within 19 months.
narrative.general_summary: Stratify automates user research with AI agents run by a two person team in San Francisco. Demand exists, but Outset, Rally and Great Question already sell to the same teams, and a two person team has limited sales capacity. In a 19 month window the B2B anchor gives a seed above $1M near 40 percent after discounting for crowding, and a Series A within the window near 8 percent given seed. Takeover risk is high because incumbents can add AI interviews within months. Odds here do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Forecast made blind from the input file only; the window runs 2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17, about 19 months.
Seed means an outside round above about $1M; the YC deal alone does not count.
Seed and Series A odds are for the window; Series B and C odds are long run conditional rates.
The Conversational AI tag cohort has 19 companies and is anecdote only.
Web search covered the market only; funding results dated after the as_of date were ignored.
